spots.title: Red Rock Roo Oasis & BLM Gateway
spots.tagline: Level pull-through gravel pad 10 mins from Arches with 30A power & dark night skies
spots.description: Welcome to our private red rock acreage nestled right along Spanish Valley, just 10 minutes south of Arches and Canyonlands. As longtime fifth-wheel travelers who explored BLM lands across the West, we built this dedicated gravel pull-through pad to welcome roaming RVers with 30A hookup, fresh potable well water, Starlink Wi-Fi, and unobstructed dark-sky milky way views. Step directly onto red rock trails from our fence line.

rigCompatibility.turnaroundSpace: Full 80ft circular driveway pad. Effortless pull-through, no backing required.
rigCompatibility.lowClearanceNotice: High clearance desert entrance. No overhead tree branches or low wires.

amenities.petRestrictions: Must be friendly and kept on leash due to local desert wildlife

proximity.attractionNote: 10 mins to Arches National Park entrance; 2 mins to Kane Creek trailhead

rules.campfirePolicy: Allowed in provided heavy steel fire ring; local fire safety rules apply

spots.title: Red Rock Juniper Ridge
spots.tagline: Panoramic red sandstone sunset vistas on 5 level pine acres
spots.description: Park your rig directly overlooking the Crimson Cliffs. As long-time Class A RVers who have driven over 200,000 miles across North America, we crafted this spot specifically to accommodate large rigs without stress. Wide 16ft crushed granite driveway, 50-amp dedicated pedestal, crystal clear well water, and unobstructed southwestern views. Come watch the sunset light up the red rocks right from your camp chairs.

rigCompatibility.turnaroundSpace: Massive turnaround pad engineered for 45ft rigs with toad vehicles.
rigCompatibility.lowClearanceNotice: No overhead obstructions; dedicated clear passage.

amenities.petRestrictions: Leashed outside; beware of local desert wildlife and cacti

proximity.attractionNote: 8 mins to Cathedral Rock Trailhead and Oak Creek swimming spots

rules.campfirePolicy: Propane fire pits only due to Coconino National Forest fire restrictions

spots.title: Whispering Pines Meadow & Creek
spots.tagline: Peaceful farm setting along Tumalo Creek with mountain views
spots.description: Pull into our organic heirloom berry farm nestled between towering Ponderosa pines and Tumalo Creek. We live here in our converted Sprinter van when not farming, so we know what rovers need: dead-level packed gravel, pure mountain spring water hookup, fast Wi-Fi for remote workers, and a bubbling creek 50 steps away to cool your feet. You are welcome to sample fresh seasonal berries when in harvest!

rigCompatibility.turnaroundSpace: Open circular driveway around the farm barn.

amenities.generatorHours: Quiet farm sanctuary — no generator use
amenities.petRestrictions: Well-behaved dogs welcome; keep on leash near chicken coop

proximity.attractionNote: 12 mins to Phil’s Trail mountain bike network and Deschutes River

rules.campfirePolicy: Allowed in farm fire bowl when Oregon Department of Forestry index allows

spots.title: Ocean Bluff Lookout & Pine Haven
spots.tagline: Coastal spruce grove overlooking harbor lobster boats at dawn
spots.description: Set your parking brake right on our granite point overlooking Frenchman Bay. As a former tugboat captain and long-time Airstreamer, I love hosting fellow road travelers. Watch the seals and lobster boats while sipping morning coffee from your rig. Features a dedicated 30A plug, fresh town water spigot, and firewood for the coastal fire pit.

rigCompatibility.turnaroundSpace: Spacious yard turn-in, easy back-in with host guidance.
rigCompatibility.lowClearanceNotice: Clear marine driveway, trimmed spruce branches.

amenities.petRestrictions: Dogs welcome, must not chase shorebirds

proximity.attractionNote: 10 mins to Acadia National Park entrance and Cadillac Mountain

rules.campfirePolicy: Shoreline stone fire pit with seasoned birch logs

spots.title: High Sierra Star Gazer Clearing
spots.tagline: Crisp alpine air, pine aroma, and off-grid mountain quiet
spots.description: An off-grid alpine haven tucked into private Jeffrey pine woods near Truckee. Designed for self-contained rigs who appreciate solar exposure, quiet nights, and stargazing at 6,200ft elevation. Level decomposed granite surface with mountain brook sounds nearby.

rigCompatibility.turnaroundSpace: Standard driveway turn, best for vans and shorter trailers.
rigCompatibility.lowClearanceNotice: Watch side tree branches on forest approach.

amenities.generatorHours: Off-grid silent zone — solar charging recommended
amenities.petRestrictions: Bear country! Pets must stay close, never left unattended

proximity.attractionNote: 15 mins to Donner Memorial State Park and Northstar trails

rules.campfirePolicy: Strict no-wood-fire zone due to California wildfire safety

spots.title: Lone Star Hill Country Vineyard Pad
spots.tagline: Wide pull-through space surrounded by live oaks and grapevines
spots.description: Pull off Highway 290 into our family vineyard estate. We installed a heavy-duty commercial crushed limestone pull-through space specifically for travelers passing through Texas wine country. Includes full 50A hookup and city potable water. Take an evening stroll through the vines under enormous Texas live oaks.

rigCompatibility.turnaroundSpace: Massive 80ft wide driveway turn around winery pavilion.
rigCompatibility.lowClearanceNotice: Trees along lane trimmed to 14ft 6in clearance.

amenities.generatorHours: 12:00 PM - 5:00 PM only if not plugged into 50A
amenities.petRestrictions: Must be on leash around tasting room grounds

proximity.attractionNote: 8 mins to Historic Main Street and Enchanted Rock State Natural Area

spots.title: Stargazer Ridge & Yucca Sanctuary
spots.tagline: Private 5-acre Mojave sanctuary with 30A solar pedestal and 360° mountain vistas
spots.description: Bask in the stillness of the high desert. Our 5-acre off-grid property sits directly adjacent to protected BLM wilderness just 12 miles from Joshua Tree National Park entrance. We provide a dead-level crushed granite pad, 30-amp solar-backed power connection, certified well water spigot, and a custom sunken fire ring with uninterrupted views of the Milky Way.

rigCompatibility.turnaroundSpace: Spacious circular turn, great for mid-size rigs and vans.
rigCompatibility.lowClearanceNotice: Completely clear desert sky, no overhead branches.

amenities.generatorHours: Silent dark sky area — solar power only
amenities.petRestrictions: Leashed pets only due to desert coyotes and cacti

proximity.attractionNote: 12 mins to West Entrance Joshua Tree National Park

rules.campfirePolicy: Propane fire bowl or strictly in sunken iron ring when calm

spots.exactAddressSecret: 6480 Desert Sun Way, Joshua Tree, CA 92252

spots.title: Smoky Mountain Laurel Creek Hollow
spots.tagline: Lush mountain forest pad beside rushing trout stream with 50A hookup
spots.description: Escape into the misty green folds of the Great Smoky Mountains. Our private 8-acre mountain homestead features a dedicated concrete pull-through pad built beside Laurel Creek. Wake up to the roar of cool mountain water and rhododendron in bloom. Features a full 50-amp pedestal, municipal spring water, and high-speed Wi-Fi.

rigCompatibility.turnaroundSpace: 75ft wide asphalt-to-concrete loop with river bend pull-through.
rigCompatibility.lowClearanceNotice: Mountain canopy trimmed to 14ft 4in along private road.

amenities.petRestrictions: Leashed at all times due to black bears and rushing creek

proximity.attractionNote: 8 mins to Great Smoky Mountains National Park Sugarlands visitor center

rules.campfirePolicy: Wood fires allowed in stone creek ring; kiln-dried firewood available

posts.title: Pacific Coast Highway 101 Dump Stations
posts.content: Here are three free municipal RV dump stations with potable water along the Oregon coast.

posts.title: Heading from Zion through Scenic Byway 12 to Moab this weekend — anyone else on the road?
posts.content: We are leaving Zion on Friday afternoon in our 28ft Class C, heading across Highway 12 toward Escalante and into Moab. Has anyone navigated the Hogsback ridge with a 28ft+ rig recently? Any specific tips on grade management and BLM boondocking spots near Boulder, UT?

comments.content: Hey Alex! Took our 35ft fifth wheel across the Hogsback last fall. Just take it slow in low gear and soak in the drop-offs on both sides — it is magnificent. You are welcome to pull into our Red Rock Roo pad in Moab for a cold water fill-up and 30A plug once you roll in!
One of the top 5 drives in the USA! Fill up diesel in Escalante before heading over Boulder Mountain. Safe roaming!

posts.title: 50-Amp vs 30-Amp hookup etiquette: What every host and guest should know
posts.content: As a long-time Class A host, I often get requests from rigs asking if they can run both AC units on a 30-amp service with a dogbone adapter. A quick tip for travelers: on 30A (3,600W max), stagger your loads! Run one AC unit at a time, especially if your electric water heater or microwave kicks on. Hosts love guests who understand how to protect their breakers.

comments.content: Great reminder Marcus! We also recommend guests use a surge protector with EMS before plugging into host pedestals. Protects both the rig and the host home electrical panel.

posts.title: Just added a level gravel extension for rigs up to 32ft at Whispering Pines!
posts.content: We spent the weekend spreading 4 loads of crushed granite by Tumalo Creek. The driveway now has an easy circular radius with no tight backing required. Berry picking season is in full swing — excited to welcome more CampRoo rovers this autumn.

posts.title: Quick roadside fix: Dealing with a sticky 12V black tank dump valve
posts.content: If your cable-actuated black tank valve starts binding when you pull into a dump station, do not force the T-handle! Spray silicone lubricant along the cable sheath under the underbelly coroplast, let it sit 5 minutes, and gently cycle it. Saved me a huge headache on the Maine turnpike yesterday.

reviews.comment: Staying at Caleb and Sarah’s red rock oasis in Moab was the highlight of our Utah parks trip! The gravel pad is dead level, 30A power ran our AC and induction cooktop flawlessly, and Caleb recommended an incredible hidden canyon sunset hike right off their back fence. This is what CampRoo is all about: true RV community hospitality.

Spectacular red sandstone cliffs right outside the camper window. Plenty of turnaround space for our van and easy gate access off Spanish Valley Dr. The well water is icy cold and delicious. We would love to host Caleb & Sarah in Bend whenever they roam the PNW!

Marcus has built an RV paradise. Unbelievable red rock views at golden hour. The 50A hookup is pristine, and having an on-site dump station saved us an hour detour. Marcus gave great advice on high-clearance backroads.

Clara and Ben were the most gracious hosts! Fresh marionberries were waiting on our arrival, and falling asleep to the sound of Tumalo Creek was pure therapy. Very easy pull-through for our 28ft Class C.
reviews.hostReply: Alex & Sam are model CampRoo members! Their rig was spotless, Jasper the pup was a delight, and we loved sharing stories around the fire bowl. Welcome back anytime!
